tools.name: buy_time
tools.description:
Buys line time by the millisecond, $0.000001 each; buying again adds time. Returns your channelId, the time bought and the time left. Then open a line with the line tool. Time you do not burn comes back on refund.
Not idempotent: each call buys more time.
Paid. With no wallet code, pay with ZEAM :: Pass: a pass (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/pass) or your own wallet (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/how-to-pay).
Example: {"ms":60000}

ms.description: milliseconds of line time; default 250. Buying again adds time

tools.name: line
tools.description:
Opens a line: calls on it spend bought time and carry no payment. op: open {channelId} takes the channelId buy_time returned and answers {nonce, sign}; sign the text in sign with the payer key (EIP-191, personal_sign); prove {channelId, nonce, signature} returns the credential; on, off, status, close {credential}. Time burns only while a call runs; an open websocket subscription burns the whole time it is open.
Example: {"op":"open","channelId":"<the channelId buy_time returned>"}

op.description: open, prove, on, off, status or close

credential.description: optional string — on, off, status, close

tools.name: get_payment_terms
tools.description:
Returns what ZEAM :: Prism costs and the three ways to pay: a pass, ZEAM :: Pass with your own wallet, or your own x402 client, or an MPP client where the 402 carries a Payment challenge. With them: the x402 quote, the price of each tool, line time and refunds. Free, no arguments.
Example: {}

tools.name: get_operator
tools.description:
Returns who runs ZEAM :: Prism, our operating theory, how we work, and how to check each claim. Free, no arguments.
Example: {}

tools.name: audit_payers
tools.description:
Who is really buying from an x402 seller on Base: each payer that opened a payment channel with the seller's escrow, and how many channels each opened. It counts the payers, not the relayers that submit their transactions.
A call without a line has only a moment, enough for a small range of recent blocks, and is cut, uncharged, when it needs longer. from_block is a block number and defaults to the whole history; Base adds about 43,200 blocks a day. The first answer says how many windows the scan will take and, at the pace of recent scans, how many milliseconds it likely takes (likely_ms) and at most on the costs recent scans met (about_ms, the time a line should hold unless the node turns slower), and each one after says how many are done and what the rest needs.
Paid, on a line: $0.000001 per millisecond. With no wallet code, ZEAM :: Pass buys the time and opens the line: a pass (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/pass) or your own wallet (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/how-to-pay).
Example: {"contract":"0x4020074e9dF2ce1deE5A9C1b5c3f541D02a10003","from_block":51000000}

contract.description: string — an x402 settlement escrow, 0x form.

receiver.description: optional string — only channels paying this receiver; omit for all.

from_block.description: optional int — first block; default the whole history. To continue a partial answer, keep it and set to_block one below its scanned.from.

to_block.description: optional int — stop; default the head.

window.description: optional int — blocks per snapshot, default 10000; smaller lands the first snapshot sooner.

line.description: Optional. A line credential, for a client that cannot send the x-line header or _meta["zeam-pass/line"]: the call runs on that line's time.

tools.name: audit_funders
tools.description:
Where a wallet's USDC on Base came from: every address that sent it USDC, with amounts, transfer counts and block ranges. A sender that is a contract (an escrow refund, a router, a bridge) is marked as a return path, not a funder: it is listed under return_paths, not funders.
A call without a line has only a moment, enough for a small range of recent blocks, and is cut, uncharged, when it needs longer. from_block is a block number and defaults to the whole history; Base adds about 43,200 blocks a day. The first answer says how many windows the scan will take and, at the pace of recent scans, how many milliseconds it likely takes (likely_ms) and at most on the costs recent scans met (about_ms, the time a line should hold unless the node turns slower), and each one after says how many are done and what the rest needs.
Paid, on a line: $0.000001 per millisecond. With no wallet code, ZEAM :: Pass buys the time and opens the line: a pass (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/pass) or your own wallet (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/how-to-pay).
Example: {"address":"0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD","from_block":51000000}

tools.name: audit_cluster
tools.description:
Whether a set of wallets on Base is one actor: who funded each with USDC, grouped by shared funder, with a verdict and the wallets it could not resolve. Turns "55 distinct payers" into "one actor with 55 wallets", or fails to. A shared funder is not counted as control when it is a contract or a distributor, an account that paid 100+ distinct recipients within the blocks scanned (an exchange hot wallet; a zero-value transfer pays no one and is not counted); dead_ends lists it with the wallets it funded and the reading names it. Whether an account is a distributor depends on the range: over fewer blocks it may have paid fewer and count.
A call without a line has only a moment, enough for a small range of recent blocks, and is cut, uncharged, when it needs longer. from_block is a block number and defaults to the whole history; Base adds about 43,200 blocks a day. The first answer says how many windows the scan will take and, at the pace of recent scans, how many milliseconds it likely takes (likely_ms) and at most on the costs recent scans met (about_ms, the time a line should hold unless the node turns slower), and each one after says how many are done and what the rest needs.
Paid, on a line: $0.000001 per millisecond. With no wallet code, ZEAM :: Pass buys the time and opens the line: a pass (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/pass) or your own wallet (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/how-to-pay).
Example: {"addresses":["0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD","0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001"],"from_block":51000000}

tools.name: call_rpc
tools.description:
Calls a JSON-RPC method on an Ethereum or Base node we run and returns the node's own answer, unchanged. Base serves eth_, net_, web3_, txpool_, debug_ and base_ methods; Ethereum serves eth_, net_, web3_, txpool_, debug_ and trace_ methods. The full list is in /llms.txt, checked against the nodes every hour.
Base is archive: state at any block. Ethereum is archive: state at any block.
Base "pending" is the next block as it builds, updated about every 200 ms (Flashblocks): eth_getBlockByNumber ["pending", true].
To stream, open the websocket at /rpc/<chain>?line=<credential> and eth_subscribe. Base: newHeads, logs, syncing, newFlashblocks, pendingLogs, newFlashblockTransactions. Ethereum: newHeads, logs, newPendingTransactions, syncing.
Send with eth_sendRawTransaction. The node holds no keys, so signing methods are refused.
Paid: $0.000001 per millisecond on a line, or $0.00025 for a call of up to 250 ms without one. With no wallet code, pay with ZEAM :: Pass: a pass (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/pass) or your own wallet (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/how-to-pay).
Example: {"chain":"base","method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[]}

chain.description: string — which node to forward to: eth or base

method.description: string — a JSON-RPC method; the ones we check are listed in /llms.txt. Not forwarded: signing methods, debug_ methods that control the node, eth_subscribe (use the websocket).

line.description: Optional. A line credential, for a client that cannot send the x-line header or _meta["zeam-pass/line"]: the call runs on that line's time.

tools.name: sample_rpc

chain.description: optional string — which node: eth or base. Default base.

method.description: optional string — one of eth_chainId, eth_blockNumber, eth_gasPrice, net_version, web3_clientVersion, net_peerCount, eth_syncing, txpool_status; default eth_blockNumber
